add_fx.description:
Add an FX plugin to a track. Works for both instruments (VSTi) and effects (VST/AU).
Use the exact plugin name as shown in REAPER's FX browser.
Built-in Cockos plugins: ReaEQ, ReaComp, ReaDelay, ReaVerb, ReaLimit, ReaSynth,
ReaSamplOmatic5000, ReaTune, ReaGate, ReaFIR, ReaXcomp.

add_master_fx.description: Add an FX plugin to the master track.

add_midi_note.description:
Add a MIDI note to an existing MIDI item.
pitch: MIDI note number 0–127 (60 = middle C, 69 = A4).
start/length: seconds, relative to the item's start.
channel: MIDI channel 0–15 (use 9 for drums).

add_pan_automation.description:
Add a pan automation point on a track, showing its pan envelope if needed.
pan: -1.0 (full left) to 1.0 (full right).

add_volume_automation.description:
Add a volume automation point on a track, showing its volume envelope if needed.
position: time in seconds. value_db: volume level in dB.

adjust_pitch.description: Adjust the pitch of an audio item by semitones (can be fractional).

adjust_playback_rate.description: Adjust playback rate of an audio item. 1.0 = normal speed, 0.5 = half speed.

analyze_dynamics.description:
Render the project and measure dynamic range: RMS, peak, crest factor,
and a simplified DR score (average peak-to-RMS over 3-second blocks).

analyze_frequency_spectrum.description:
Render the project and analyze frequency band levels.
Returns RMS level in dB for seven bands:
sub_bass (20–60Hz), bass (60–250Hz), low_mids (250–500Hz),
mids (500–2kHz), high_mids (2–4kHz), presence (4–8kHz), brilliance (8–20kHz).

analyze_loudness.description:
Render the project to a temp file and measure integrated loudness (LUFS)
and true peak (dBTP) using the ITU-R BS.1770 standard.

analyze_stereo_field.description:
Render the project and analyze stereo width and mono compatibility.
Returns mid/side balance, stereo width ratio, and L/R correlation.
Correlation near 1 = mono-like, near 0 = wide stereo, negative = phase issues.

analyze_transients.description:
Render the project and detect transient events (note attacks, drum hits, etc.).
Returns the count and timing of up to 100 transient onset events.

apply_limiter.description:
Add ReaLimit to the master track and set its threshold and release.
threshold_db: -60 to +12 dB.
release_db_per_sec: how fast gain reduction recovers, in dB per second as
ReaLimit displays it (about 6 and up; higher recovers faster; default 15).

apply_mastering_chain.description:
Add a standard mastering FX chain to the master track.
Presets: default (EQ > Comp > Limiter), loud (EQ > Comp x2 > Limiter),
gentle (EQ > light Comp > Limiter).
After applying, use set_master_fx_parameter to dial in specific settings.
Use list_master_fx + get_fx_parameters to discover parameter indices.

arm_track.description:
Arm (or disarm) a track for recording. Arming does not start recording.
exclusive: also disarm every other track, so only this one records.

bypass_fx.description: Enable or bypass (disable) an FX plugin on a track.

check_input_level.description:
Listen to an armed track's input for a few seconds (0.5 to 10) and say whether
the level is right to record: "no signal" (with things to check), "too quiet",
"good" or "clipping". Play or sing as loud as you will in the take while it
listens. Reports the peak level in dBFS (aim for about -12). Never starts recording.
track_index: the track to check; by default the only armed track.

create_bus.description:
Create a new bus track and route the given tracks to it via sends.
track_indices: list of track indices to feed into the bus.
The routed tracks stop sending straight to the master (or to their parent
folder), so they are heard once, through the bus, instead of twice.
The bus is added at the end, outside any folder.

create_chord_progression.description:
Create a chord progression on a track as a single MIDI item.
chords: comma-separated chord names, e.g. "C,G,Am,F" or "Cm7,Fm7,Bb7,Ebmaj7".
Supports: maj, min/m, dim, aug, maj7, min7/m7, dom7/7, dim7, hdim7, sus2, sus4.
All chords are voiced around middle C (MIDI 60).

create_drum_pattern.description:
Create a drum pattern on a track using a step-sequencer string.
Each character = one step. Characters: k=kick, s=snare, h=hihat(closed),
o=hihat(open), t=tom(low), m=tom(mid), f=tom(high), c=crash, r=ride, .=rest.
Example 4/4 rock beat (16 steps): "k...h...s...h..."
All drum notes are placed on MIDI channel 9 (GM standard).

create_midi_item.description: Create an empty MIDI item on a track. Returns item_id for use with add_midi_note.

create_project.description:
Create a new REAPER project in a new project tab. The current project stays
open in its own tab, unsaved changes included.
use_default_template: start from the default project template set in REAPER's
preferences (its tracks, routing and settings); without one configured the
project starts empty. false: always start empty.
tempo / time_signature (e.g. "3/4"): set them; when omitted a template keeps
its own, and an empty project gets 120 BPM 4/4 with use_default_template=false.
name: the song's name; save_project uses it as the file name on the first save.

create_send.description: Create an aux send from one track to another.

create_track.description:
Create a new track at the end of the project.
track_type: audio, midi, instrument, folder.
midi and instrument tracks record from every MIDI device on every channel.
Instrument tracks also have input monitoring on: once the track is armed for
recording, playing the keyboard sounds through the instrument plugin (add it
with add_fx). A track that is not armed stays silent while you play.

crop_to_active_take.description:
Delete every take of an item except the active one (undo brings them
back; the files stay on disk). Choose the take first with set_active_take.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

delete_item.description:
Delete an item from its track (undo brings it back).
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

delete_track.description:
Delete a track.
track_index: the track's index, or its GUID from list_tracks (safer: a GUID
still names the same track after tracks were added, deleted or moved).

detect_clipping.description:
Render the project and detect digital clipping (samples at or above 0 dBFS).
Returns clipped sample count, peak level in dB, and whether clipping was found.

duplicate_item.description:
Copy an item (with all its takes, fades and settings) as a new item with
new GUIDs. position: where the copy starts (seconds; default right after the
original). dest_track_index: the track for the copy (default the same track).
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

edit_audio_item.description:
Legacy: prefer edit_item (exact start/end and fades, items named by GUID).
Trim an audio item by relative amounts and/or add fades. All values in seconds.
start_trim: seconds to remove from the beginning.
end_trim: seconds to remove from the end.
fade_in/fade_out: fade length in seconds. Unlike edit_item, 0 here leaves
the fade as it is (edit_item fade_in=0 removes it).

edit_item.description:
Set an item's settings to exact values; anything left out stays as it is.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.
start/end: where the item starts/ends (project seconds); the audio stays where
it is in time, so this trims (or uncovers) the item's edges. To move the
whole item use move_item.
fade_in/fade_out: fade length in seconds, 0 removes the fade.
volume_db: the item's own volume, the one to use for "make this louder/quieter".
take_volume_db: the active take's volume, which normalize_item sets; usually
leave it alone. Both add up, and the track's volume comes on top.
muted, locked: locked=false unlocks a locked item (and allows the other changes).

get_audio_setup.description:
The audio interface REAPER is using: audio system (JACK, ALSA...), input
and output device, sample rate, block size, sample format (bits), whether audio is
running, the input and output channels (numbered from 1, with names) and the
input/output latency in samples and milliseconds. The device cannot be
changed through the API: how_to_change says where to change it in REAPER.

get_context.description:
What is happening in REAPER right now: play state, edit cursor and play
position (seconds), time selection and loop range (null when empty), whether
repeat is on, REAPER's punch mode, metronome and count-in (null if unknown),
the selected tracks and items (with GUIDs), the FX touched last,
whether the project has unsaved changes, and the project file ("" if never saved).

get_fx_parameters.description: Get all parameters for an FX plugin, including names, indices, and current values.

get_project_info.description:
Get basic information about the current project: name, file, recording
folder, tempo, track count, length, markers and regions. For every track's
routing, recording setup and FX use get_project_summary.

get_project_summary.description:
The whole project in one call: name, file, tempo, time signature, length,
the master (volume, FX), and every track with its GUID, name, volume (dB), pan,
mute/solo, record arm, record input, input monitoring, FX names, sends and item
count; plus markers and regions.

get_track_info.description:
Get detailed information about a track including FX, items and its
recording setup (armed, record input, monitoring, record mode).

get_undo_state.description:
Say what undo and redo would do right now: the name of the step undo would
take back (next_undo) and the one redo would bring back (next_redo), or null.
Steps made by this server start with "MCP: ".

glue_items.description:
Glue items of one track into a single item playing a new audio file that
REAPER renders (into the project's recording folder). The originals are
replaced; gaps between them become silence. What you hear is baked into the
new file: the active take only, its take FX, item and take volume, and fades.
Items with more than one take are refused (crop_to_active_take first). Rarely
needed: splits, moves and remove_silence work without gluing.
items_to_glue: the items' GUIDs from list_items (preferred), or their
indices on track_index.

import_audio_file.description:
Import an audio file onto a track at the given position (seconds).
Supports all formats REAPER can read: wav, aiff, mp3, flac, ogg, etc.

insert_track_template.description:
Insert a saved track template into the current project, exactly like REAPER's own
"Insert track from template": FX with their saved state, routing, folder structure,
envelopes and items are all preserved. Templates can contain several tracks.
template: a name or path from list_track_templates ("Vocal Chain", "Vocals/Lead Vox"),
          or an absolute path to a .RTrackTemplate file.
position: 0-based track index the template's first track should occupy. Existing
          tracks at that index and below are shifted down. Omit to append at the end.
The inserted tracks are left selected, matching REAPER's behaviour.

list_items.description:
List the items of every track, or of one track: GUID, track, item index,
position and length (seconds), muted, locked, take count, the active take's
name and whether it is MIDI; on REAPER 7 fixed-lane tracks also the item's
lane and whether that lane plays. detail=true adds fade lengths (manual and
automatic crossfade, seconds), item volume (dB), and the active take's start
offset, playrate, volume (dB) and source file.

list_master_fx.description: List all FX plugins on the master track.

list_project_templates.description:
List the project templates (.RPP files in REAPER's ProjectTemplates folder,
subfolders included) that new_project_from_template can start from.

list_sends.description:
List all sends from a track: the destination track (index, GUID, name),
volume in dB, pan and mute.

list_takes.description:
List an item's takes: index, name, GUID, which one is active (plays),
source file, start offset, playrate and take volume (dB). On a REAPER 7
fixed-lane track also the overlapping lanes (lane number, whether it plays,
the lane item's GUID).
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

list_track_fx.description: List all FX plugins on a track.

list_track_templates.description:
List the track templates (.RTrackTemplate files) in REAPER's TrackTemplates folder,
including subfolders. Each entry has 'name' (file name without extension), 'path'
(relative to the TrackTemplates folder, e.g. "Vocals/Lead Vox"), the absolute 'file',
and the names of the tracks the template contains.
Pass either 'name' or 'path' to insert_track_template.

list_tracks.description:
List all tracks in the current project with their basic parameters and
recording setup (armed, record input, monitoring, record mode); compact:
get_project_summary adds routing and FX names.

load_fx_preset.description: Load a saved preset by name for an FX plugin.

load_project.description:
Open a REAPER project (.rpp) from the given file path in place of the
current one. Refuses while the current project has unsaved changes: save it
first (save_project), or open a new tab with create_project.

move_item.description:
Move a whole item (its audio with it) in time and/or to another track.
position: the new start (seconds); dest_track_index: the track to move it to.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

new_project_from_template.description:
Start a new project from a project template, in a new project tab (the
current project stays open in its tab). template: a name from
list_project_templates, or the path of a .RPP file. The new project is
untitled: save it with save_project before recording. Each call opens
another tab, so do not retry it just to be sure.

normalize_item.description:
Normalize an audio item by setting its active take's volume so the
recording, together with the item's own volume, reaches target_db.
mode "peak": loudest sample at target_db dBFS (default -1). mode "lufs":
integrated loudness at target_db LUFS (default -18, a comfortable level for
mixing). Take FX and the track's volume still apply on top. Only the take
volume changes; the file is untouched.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

normalize_project.description:
Measure the project's integrated loudness, then adjust the master volume
so the output hits the target LUFS level.
Common targets: -14 LUFS (streaming), -16 LUFS (podcasts), -23 LUFS (broadcast).

play_project.description: Start project playback from the current cursor position.

redo.description:
Redo the last undone change, like Ctrl+Shift+Z in REAPER, and say which
step was redone. Like undo, only redoes this server's steps unless
include_manual_steps=true, and never while recording.

remove_fx.description:
Remove an FX plugin from a track by its index.
track_index: the track's index, or its GUID from list_tracks (safer: a GUID
still names the same track after tracks were added, deleted or moved).

remove_send.description:
Remove a send from a track by its index (see list_sends).
source_track_index: the track's index, or its GUID from list_tracks (safer: a
GUID still names the same track after tracks were added, deleted or moved).

remove_silence.description:
Remove the silent parts of an audio item: it is split around each stretch
quieter than threshold_db (RMS dBFS of the recording, before item volume)
lasting at least min_silence seconds, and those pieces are deleted.
padding: seconds of quiet kept next to the sound, so breaths and note tails
are not cut. fade: a short fade (seconds) where sound was cut, against clicks.
dry_run=true only reports what would be removed (ranges, total seconds and how
many pieces would stay). Raise threshold_db (e.g. -35) for a noisy recording;
lower it (e.g. -55) if quiet notes get cut. Only the active take is analyzed.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.
Returns the removed time ranges and the GUIDs of the pieces kept.

render_project.description:
Render the entire project to a file. An existing file is only replaced
with overwrite=true.
format: wav, flac, mp3 (requires LAME), ogg.
sample_rate: e.g. 44100, 48000, 96000.
bit_depth: 16, 24, or 32 (WAV only; ignored for mp3/ogg/flac).
channels: 1 (mono) or 2 (stereo).

render_regions.description:
Render each region of the project to its own file, using the project's
render settings.
pattern: file name pattern; $region, $regionnumber, $project are available,
    and it may name subdirectories. REAPER numbers names that would clash
    ("take-001", "take-002").
selected_only: render only the regions selected in REAPER; with none
    selected, REAPER renders all of them.
dry_run: return the project's regions and the files REAPER would write,
    without rendering. It sets the render settings and restores them.
Fails without rendering if any output file already exists; never deletes files.
Blocks until every file is written; status is then "complete". Gives up
with "stalled" once the files stop growing for stall_timeout_seconds
(longer while REAPER holds a scratch file), or "timeout" after
timeout_seconds in total.
Region "index" is the position among regions, as in get_project_info.

render_stems.description:
Render each track as a separate stem file by soloing each track individually.
track_indices: list of track indices, or null to render all tracks.
Files are named after the track names in the output directory. Existing
files are only replaced with overwrite=true.

render_time_selection.description:
Render a specific time range of the project to a file. An existing file
is only replaced with overwrite=true.

save_project.description:
Save the current project as a .rpp file, which then becomes the open
project's file (later saves and new recordings go next to it). With no path,
a project that has a file is saved to it again; one that was never saved gets
a new file in the documents folder's "REAPER Projects" folder, named after the
project (name from create_project, else the time), with " (2)" added if that
name is taken. An existing file at a given path is only replaced with
overwrite=true. The reply's project_path is the file written.

save_project_template.description:
Save the current project as a project template named name (in REAPER's
ProjectTemplates folder), to start new songs from with new_project_from_template.
The open project keeps its own file. An existing template is only replaced with
overwrite=true. A project with items (recordings, MIDI) is refused unless
include_items=true: every new song would start with them. Remove them first
for a clean template.

save_track_template.description:
Save tracks (with their FX, input, routing between them and settings) as a
track template named name in REAPER's TrackTemplates folder, for
insert_track_template. track_indices: the tracks to save; by default the
selected ones. include_items: also save their items. The track selection is
left as it was. An existing template is only replaced with overwrite=true.

set_active_take.description:
Choose which take of an item plays (take_index, from list_takes); the
other takes are kept. (On a REAPER 7 fixed-lane track, choose the playing
lane in REAPER itself.)
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

set_cursor_position.description: Move the edit cursor to a position in seconds.

set_fx_parameter.description:
Set a normalized parameter value (0.0–1.0) on an FX plugin.
Use get_fx_parameters to discover available parameters and their indices.

set_loop.description:
Turn repeat (looped playback) on or off. start/end (seconds, both or
neither): also set the loop range. Turning repeat on needs a loop range.
Reports the time selection too: REAPER usually links it to the loop range.

set_master_fx_parameter.description: Set a normalized parameter (0.0–1.0) on a master track FX plugin.

set_master_volume.description: Set the master track output volume in dB.

set_metronome.description:
Turn the metronome (click) on or off; leave enabled out to only report it.
Also reports count_in (REAPER plays the click for a bar or two before it
starts recording; null if unknown). Count-in cannot be changed from here:
right-click the metronome button on REAPER's transport bar and tick
"Count-in before recording".

set_monitoring.description:
Input monitoring: hear what the track's input receives, through REAPER.
mode: "off", "on", or "tape" (heard while stopped and recording, not while
playing back). Use headphones when it is on (see the warning in the reply).

set_punch_mode.description:
How recording starts and stops, for every project: REAPER keeps this
option on, in later projects and sessions too, until it is set back to normal.
mode: "normal" (records from the moment you start until you stop) or
"time_selection" (auto-punch: plays the whole time but only records inside the
time selection; set it first with set_time_selection).

set_recording_format.description:
The file format new recordings are written in. REAPER's default (WAV,
24-bit) is already right for most recording; change it only if asked.
format: "wav" or "flac" (lossless and smaller; REAPER's default FLAC settings).
bit_depth (WAV only): 24 (recommended), 16, or 32 (32-bit float).

set_send_volume.description: Set the volume of a send in dB.

set_tempo.description: Set the project tempo in BPM.

set_time_selection.description:
Select the time from start to end (seconds). start == end clears the
selection. Auto-punch recording (set_punch_mode) records only inside it.
Reports the loop range too: REAPER usually links it to the time selection.

set_time_signature.description: Set the project time signature, e.g. 4/4, 3/4, 6/8.

set_track_color.description: Set track color using RGB values (0–255 each).

set_track_input.description:
Choose what a track records from.
input: "mono" (one input, numbered from 1: channel), "stereo" (inputs channel and
channel+1), "midi" (every MIDI device; midi_channel 0 = all channels, or 1-16)
or "none". On a Focusrite Scarlett Solo input 1 is the microphone (XLR) socket
and input 2 the instrument/line socket, so a guitar is mono channel=2.
Audio inputs are checked against the interface's input count.

set_track_pan.description: Set track pan. -1.0 = full left, 0.0 = center, 1.0 = full right.

set_track_record_mode.description:
What an armed track records (per track; the punch mode is set_punch_mode).
Most recording needs no change: "input" is the default.
mode: "input" (the input: voice, guitar, keyboard; the usual choice),
"output" (the track's own stereo output, FX included), "midi_overdub" (add
notes to existing MIDI items), "midi_replace" (replace the notes where you
play) or "none" (armed for monitoring only, records nothing).

set_track_volume.description: Set track volume in dB. Range: roughly -150 to +12 dB.

split_item.description:
Split an item at one or more times (project seconds, each inside the item
and at least 1 ms from its edges; times closer than 1 ms count once).
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.
Returns the pieces left to right with their GUIDs; the first keeps the
original GUID, the others are new items.

start_recording.description:
Start recording, after checking it can work: not already recording, audio
running, the project saved (so takes are stored next to it), and each track
that will record has an input and a record mode that records. Playback is
stopped first, so the take starts at position.
track_index: the track to record on (armed here); by default the tracks
already armed. disarm_others: disarm every other track, so nothing else is
recorded by accident. position: start from here (seconds) instead of the edit
cursor. save_first: save a never-saved project instead of refusing.
Warns about monitoring, auto-punch and repeat. Stop with stop_recording.

stop_recording.description:
Stop recording and keep everything recorded (no dialog asks what to do with
the files). Reports each new take: track, item, position and length (seconds),
file, and its peak level in dBFS with clipped=true where it hit 0 dBFS.
To throw a take away afterwards, call undo with include_manual_steps=true.

stop_transport.description:
Stop playback. While recording, prefer stop_recording: it also lists the
new takes. (A recording stopped here is kept too, without a dialog.)

suggest_best_take.description:
Check an item's takes (or, on a REAPER 7 fixed-lane track, its lanes) for
technical problems: clipping, a very low level, and sound that stops early
or starts late compared with the others. Suggests a take only when exactly
one has the fewest problems; otherwise lists the tied ones ("tied"). Louder
is not better: it cannot judge the performance, so listen before choosing,
then use set_active_take. Nothing is changed.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

trim_item_to_time_selection.description:
Trim an item to the time selection: the parts before and after it are
removed and the audio that stays does not move in time.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.
Set the time selection first with set_time_selection.

trim_silence.description:
Trim the silence at the start and end of an audio item (nothing in the
middle is touched); the audio that stays does not move in time.
threshold_db: RMS dBFS of the recording below which it counts as silence.
padding: seconds of quiet kept before the first and after the last sound.
item: the item's GUID from list_items (preferred), or its index on track_index.

undo.description:
Undo the last change in the project, like Ctrl+Z in REAPER, and say which
step was undone. Every change this server makes is one step ("MCP: ..."), so
one undo takes back one whole tool call.
Only this server's steps are undone: when the last step was made by hand in
REAPER or is recorded media (undoing it deletes the take just recorded), the
tool refuses and names it; pass include_manual_steps=true only after the user
confirms. Never undoes while recording.
